children: South Africa’s 10-year government bond yield rose above 8.80%, close to the highest since mid-September, supported by expectations of additional policy tightening.
The South African Reserve Bank raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 7.25%, as expected, and signalled the possibility of further increases this year.
The move follows a 25-basis-point rate cut by the Federal Reserve last week.
Governor Lesetja Kganyago said the central bank sees upside risks to inflation alongside downside risks to growth.
Volatile global fuel prices remain a key risk amid the ongoing Middle East conflict, while food and core goods inflation pressures have been more subdued.

Headline inflation is expected to rise above 5% later this year and into early 2027 before easing as the impact of higher fuel prices fades, with inflation projected to return to around 3% by the end of 2027.

title: South Africa 10-Year Bond Yield Inches Higher
